dossier.headline: Foreign investors extend a record-setting buying run
dossier.summary: Foreign institutional investors have been net buyers of Indian shares for seven straight sessions, including a near six-year single-day high of about ₹14,975 crore on November 5. Domestic institutions have sold into the buying, roughly matching Monday's ₹7,212 crore FII inflow with about ₹7,173 crore of net sales.
why_it_matters: Sustained foreign buying has been the main support for large caps this month
Domestic funds taking profits offsets much of the inflow
watch: Whether the streak survives hotter US inflation and higher US yields
questions: How long can foreign buying continue at this pace?
Why are domestic funds selling into the rally?
conflicts: NSDL data showed about ₹38,971 crore of November FPI inflows by Nov 9, a different measure from the exchange provisional figures
